title: The derived-limit counit recovers a compatible tower family from its cone lift
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be the category of modules on a small ringed site [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and let $C_\bullet=(C_m,t_m)$ be a strict inverse tower of complexes. Choose a K-injective tower resolution $q:C_\bullet\to I_\bullet$ whose terms $I^p_\bullet$ are injective objects of the category of strict towers [def-pur-kinjective-complex, def-sp-injective-resolutions, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], so that $R\lim C_\bullet=\lim I_\bullet$ [def-weil-derived-limit] and the inclusion $\iota:\lim I_\bullet\to\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1](I_\bullet)$, with zero shifted-product component, is a quasi-isomorphism. Let $\epsilon_C:\Delta R\lim C_\bullet\to C_\bullet$ be the derived-limit counit in the derived category of strict towers, namely $[q]^{-1}$ composed with the ordinary limit-cone map $\Delta\lim I_\bullet\to I_\bullet$. If $P$ is a complex and $\theta_m:P\to C_m$ is a compatible family, $t_m\circ\theta_{m+1}=\theta_m$, write $\theta^\Delta:\Delta P\to C_\bullet$ for the induced strict tower map and $\tilde\theta:P\to\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1](C_\bullet)$ for the cone lift $z\mapsto(0,(\theta_m(z))_m)$. Let $r_\theta=[\iota]^{-1}\circ[\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1](q)\circ\tilde\theta]:P\to R\lim C_\bullet$. Then in the derived category of strict towers
$$\epsilon_C\circ\Delta(r_\theta)=\theta^\Delta.$$
Thus the cone lift realizes the given compatible family at every level; the equality is before applying any further functor or passing to individual quotient derived categories, and no exactness of countable products is assumed.

proof.text: We first prove the assertion of the statement that $\iota$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Fix a degree $p$ and write $J=I^p_\bullet$, an injective object of $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$ with transitions $t^J_n:J_{n+1}\to J_n$. For an object $F$ of $\mathcal A$ and $n\geq1$ let $T_n(F)$ be the tower equal to $F$ at levels $1,\ldots,n$ with identity transitions there and $0$ above $n$. A tower map $T_n(F)\to J$ is determined by its level-$n$ component $F\to J_n$, the lower components being forced to be the transitions composed with it; conversely every map $F\to J_n$ arises. The map $T_n(F)\to T_{n+1}(F)$ which is the identity at levels $\leq n$ and $0\to F$ at level $n+1$ is a tower map and is levelwise monic, hence a monomorphism of $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$ by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Restriction along it sends the tower map with top component $\psi:F\to J_{n+1}$ to the one with level-$n$ component $t^J_n\psi$. Taking $F=J_n$ and the map corresponding to $\mathrm{id}_{J_n}$, injectivity of $J$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions] gives $\sigma_n:J_n\to J_{n+1}$ with $t^J_n\sigma_n=\mathrm{id}_{J_n}$. Let $\Pi^p=\prod_mJ_m$ (products of module sheaves exist, computed sectionwise) and define $\tau:\Pi^p\to\Pi^p$ by the product universal property with $\mathrm{pr}_1\tau=0$ and recursively $\mathrm{pr}_{n+1}\tau=\sigma_n(\mathrm{pr}_n\tau-\mathrm{pr}_n)$. Then $\mathrm{pr}_n(1-s)\tau=\mathrm{pr}_n\tau-t^J_n\mathrm{pr}_{n+1}\tau=\mathrm{pr}_n$, so $(1-s)\tau=\mathrm{id}$ and $1-s:\prod_mI_m\to\prod_mI_m$ is an epimorphism in every degree; $\tau$ need not commute with differentials and is used only degreewise. The degreewise kernel of $1-s$ consists of the compatible families, i.e. it is the termwise inverse limit $\lim_mI_m$ with its inclusion into the product. Since $1-s$ is a chain map (the differentials of $I_\bullet$ commute with transitions), [lem-weil-degreewise-epi-kernel-cocone-qis] applied to $f=1-s$ says that the map with zero shifted-product component and the kernel inclusion as product component, which is $\iota$, is a quasi-isomorphism $\lim I_\bullet\to\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1](I_\bullet)$. No exactness of countable products is used.

proof.text: Let $\bar\theta:P\to\lim_m I_m$ be the unique chain map whose $m$-th projection is $q_m\circ\theta_m$. The maps $q_m\circ\theta_m$ are compatible because $q$ is a strict map of towers and the family $\theta_m$ satisfies $t_m\circ\theta_{m+1}=\theta_m$. Thus the ordinary termwise inverse-limit universal property gives $\bar\theta$, and its uniqueness is part of that universal property. The termwise inverse-limit model computes $R\lim C_\bullet$ for the chosen K-injective tower resolution by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit].

proof.text:
Put $H_I=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1](I_\bullet)$. On the strict chain level, $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1](q)\circ\widetilde\theta$ has zero shifted-product component and product component $(q_m\circ\theta_m)_m$. By the definition of $\bar\theta$ in Step 2, the inclusion $\iota$ with zero shifted-product component has exactly the same two components after composing with $\bar\theta$. Hence
$$\iota\circ\bar\theta=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1](q)\circ\widetilde\theta.$$
The compatibility equations make $(1-s)(q_m\theta_m)_m=0$, so both sides are indeed chain maps; this coordinate calculation uses no exactness of countable products.

source.place: Tag 0941, explicit Roos cone map and compatible-family calculation

proof.text:
Passing the equality of Step 3 to the derived category and using the quasi-isomorphism $\iota$ of Step 1, we obtain
$$[\iota]^{-1}\circ[\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1](q)\circ\widetilde\theta]=[\bar\theta].$$
By the definition of $r_\theta$, this says $r_\theta=[\bar\theta]$.

source.place: Tag 0941, derived-category realization of the Roos cone

proof.text:
Let $\lambda_I:\Delta\lim_m I_m\to I_\bullet$ be the ordinary limit-cone map. For every level $m$, the $m$-component of $\lambda_I\circ\Delta(\bar\theta)$ is the projection of $\bar\theta$, namely $q_m\circ\theta_m$. The $m$-component of $q\circ\theta^\Delta$ is also $q_m\circ\theta_m$. Equality of strict tower maps is levelwise, so
$$\lambda_I\circ\Delta(\bar\theta)=q\circ\theta^\Delta.$$

source.place: Tag 0941, naturality of the ordinary limit cone with compatible maps

proof.text:
The counit in the statement is $\epsilon_C=[q]^{-1}\circ[\lambda_I]$. Combining this definition with Steps 4 and 5 gives
$$\epsilon_C\circ\Delta(r_\theta)=[q]^{-1}\circ[\lambda_I]\circ\Delta([\bar\theta])=[q]^{-1}\circ[q]\circ[\theta^\Delta]=[\theta^\Delta].$$
Thus the equality holds in the derived category of strict towers, before any further functor or passage to individual quotient derived categories.
